themes_detail.label: Street lights failing across district
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints spiked to 26 THIS WEEK, up 352% from the 5.8-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.49), suggesting a potential citywide infrastructure failure or localized grid issue affecting public safety and visibility in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 26 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.49 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Community board has repeatedly requested DOT capital funds for infrastructure repair—systemic underinvestment may be materializing
reporting_angles: Contact DOT to determine if this is a grid failure, maintenance backlog, or equipment defect; compare to citywide data
Document public safety impact: interview residents about safety concerns at night; check NYPD crime data for correlation with dark blocks

themes_detail.label: Food poisoning cluster emerges
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.2 weekly average—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting either a contaminated food source, outbreak at a local establishment, or sudden reporting surge worth investigating for public health risk.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.35 indicates highly significant deviation
Community board has standing requests for public health program funding—underlying capacity may be stretched
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint details to pinpoint affected establishments; cross-reference with NYC Health Department inspection records and violations
Interview affected residents about symptoms, timing, and food source; contact NYC Health Department to ask if they've detected a pattern

themes_detail.label: Non-emergency police calls surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints rose to 7 THIS WEEK, up 229% from the 2.1 weekly baseline—a statistically significant spike (z-score: 4.63)—indicating either rising quality-of-life issues or increased resident reporting of low-level incidents.
evidence: 7 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (229% increase)
Coincides with encampment complaints 3 weeks ago (9 vs. 1.4 avg), suggesting ongoing quality-of-life pressures
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint details to categorize what non-emergency issues residents are reporting; look for patterns (loitering, harassment, disorder)
Interview local residents and business owners about perceived safety and quality-of-life changes; query NYPD about response patterns

themes_detail.label: Encampment reports spike remains elevated
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 9 (554% above the 1.4 weekly baseline, z-score: 5.1), signaling a visible homelessness surge or inadequate outreach capacity that aligns with the community board's long-standing requests for services to vulnerable populations.
evidence: 9 encampment complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (554% spike)
Community board has repeated, unfunded requests for outreach services to vulnerable adults—structural gap may be widening
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations from 311 data; interview residents and local advocates about scale and duration of visible homelessness
Contact Department for the Aging and DHS to determine why community board funding requests go unmet; audit outreach capacity in CD109

themes_detail.label: Rodent complaints remain high
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 15 three weeks ago, 173% above the 5.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.25), and remain elevated, indicating either a seasonal surge, structural building failures, or sanitation gaps compounded by the district's chronic unsanitary condition complaints (715 over 90 days).
evidence: 15 rodent complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 5.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (173% increase)
Unsanitary condition complaints total 715 over 90 days, suggesting underlying property maintenance and sanitation infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Cross-reference rodent complaints with plumbing (749), water leak (396), and paint/plaster (611) complaints to identify buildings with multiple code violations
Interview DOE and HPD inspectors about enforcement patterns; identify repeat offender buildings and interview tenants about conditions
